questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different aspects that I found important when choosing my destination. First of all I chose Canada since I have been very fascinated by the country and would like to go there and experience their culture and learn about the country. I have also heard that University of Toronto (UofT) is a very good university and I therefore hope that it can have a small effect on future carrier options that I went there for a semester. However, for most part it was important that I chose a destination that I found very attractive and where the culture and values reminded me slightly of back home, so I wouldn't feel too foreign in a place I had to live in for four months.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My overall study abroad experience was amazing, but UofT was absolutely horrible at facilitating meet-ups for exchange students... I, and all the others were extremely lucky that we figured it out ourselves, but UofT made no effort what so ever in contributing to our social lives.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was really easy... It's been a while since then, but I don't recall I had any problems with finding the necessary information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was a member of a Facebook group for all exchange students that helped a lot and provided some information, but otherwise we were a lot left on our own. UofT's systems however was quite easy to navigate in after everything had been set up (Student card etc.)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
I don't know if all this is a lot due to covid... All orientation was online which might have impacted my experience a lot. I have no clue on who to write if I had any problems, but there wasn't any major problems I couldn't solve myself, and they had some clear how-too's on their website on how to set up all the UofT-platforms etc., that was really helpful.

A good thing to remember is that you can always write to the student-exchange mail, and then they will help you. That's what they are for.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: On UofT's website I managed to find their off campus housing suggestions and I just applied at some of those places. I lived at Neill-Wycik Student Coop Resident downtown near Ryerson University (fyi. the name of this university is about to be changed, so it will have another name in the future). It worked out pretty well for me, and I was glad I found the place before I moved to Toronto. A recommendation would be to start looking for housing right after you get you acceptance letter. Then you don't have to stress and have a lot of time.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would definetly recommend living off-campus since it is much cheaper. However you have to buy all your meals yourself of course (not a problem if you are used to that), since there are no meal plans. You should also know that you might have to bring/buy a lot of kitchen and cleaning supplies etc. yourself. You can't count on those things being there. Furthermore, I was lucky that my off-campus housing was a student resident as well, or cooperative living, but you might have to find your social live elsewhere if you choose off-campus housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As an exchange student you just receive a mail on how to register for courses. The registration process itself was really easy, but finding out what kind of courses I was allowed to take was reallt difficult. However, they also had a guide in the top of their registration process, which made it so much easier. Overall, if you just take your time to understand the system, then it really isn't difficult, but actually quite intuitive.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't remember needing help for registration so I actually don't know... But there is always the exchange mail you can write to and get some help if needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful. I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time to understand their system, then it's quite easy... And registre as quick as possible for the courses you are sure you want. Some courses fill up quite fast, so the faster you are the more sure you'll be you get the courses you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the courses difficulty at UofT very fitting for me. I primarily chose 200level courses, which is second year courses on the BA and therefore were supposed to be lower level than what I am (I went on fifth semester, meaning third year), but I think it's important to remember that your classes aren't taught in your native language. It wasn't hard to follow, but I found the level I chose very fitting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I feel like I was thrown back to High-school some days (Gymnasiet). We had to do some assignments in each course during the semester as well as tests or discussion posts. I felt like we were kept an eye on all the time, which I am not sure I liked... But at the same time it was a way of ensuring that we kept up with the class and readings. Then our final grade is a mix of how well we did in these different aspects during the semester. It was definetly a lot different than the style of teaching at UCPH where everyone just have to perform at the exams... There are pros and cons on both teaching styles I think, but it was difficult getting used to in the beginning.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Sociology of Crime and Deviance (SOC212H1 F), Urban Sociology (SOC205H1 F), Introduction to Environmental Studies (ENV100H1 F).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Urban Sociology was a nice course. It was really interesting and I feel I gained a lot of new knowledge. - The same for Sociology of Crime and Deviance, however I didn't really like the professor and also found the course really stressful because the tests we had to do was terrible.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I had any unexpected costs actually... A small thing could be that you always forget that the prices listed (on everything!!) is without tax (around 13%) and you ALWAYS have to tip... So things in general were always a different price than at first anticipated.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries were a lot more expensive for some reason in Canada... Especially vegetables.
Their phone services (Canadian SIM-card) is also way too expensive in my opinion.
Coffee was on the otherhand a lot cheaper and dining out in general slightly cheaper than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a lot of different options for sports and working out. But that's it. I think they might have a lot of cultural and social options as well, but because of Covid I think the different offers weren't too visible.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do some sports! Go with some other exchange students and try some different things out.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Niagara Falls is of course a must, and I think it is quite easy to go Algonquin National Park or Montreal for a weekend, but actually I would suggest just to explore Toronto. Go to Toronto Islands, visit clubs and bars and restaurants, the distillery district, and the CN tower with some of your new exchange-friends from other countries. Don't look at exchange as you have to see the entire country you are visiting, because that's not possible. Instead, just try to get the experience of living and feeling at home in another city. That experience is quite remarkable as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy since Canada is also largely a part of the Western culture. However, the locals always start a sentence with "Hi, how are you doing", and you should just answer "I'm fine, how are you doing", but don't expect anymore than that. They are just being polite.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't do that a lot, I primarily hung out with other exchange students from other countries, so unfortunately, no.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences challenging, I think.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I don't really know... Maybe I appreciated that it reminded me largely of Denmark so I could focus on getting to know the people and the country instead of thinking of how to fit in.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't use too much time on studying... A big part of going on exchange is also experiencing the culture and getting to know a lot of exchange students from other countries. - Networking!
2. You are left a lot to yourself, and even though there are mails you can write to for help you should be prepared to figure a lot of things out yourself. It can be challenging but also very valuable in the end to know that you did it.
3. Choose to study at St. George campus if possible! UofT has three campuses, but the other two (Scarborough and Missisauga) are a bit fare out of Toronto. St. George is in the middle of Toronto and close to downtown, which is where you want to be.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of people say that you should go on exchange alone/by yourself, but I went with two other girls from my study at UCPH... It was a coincidence, but for me it was the best decision to go with someone I slightly knew... It helped me a lot. So do what's best for you and don't let other tell you that it is wrong to go with someone you know in advance. As long as you are still open-minded and willing to get to know new people and hang out with them as well.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Might be a bit of a cliche, but I had some personal problems before going so that I got through my exchange and still see it as an amazing experience is a huge victory for me.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being fare away from my best friends and family for four months and feeling really alone sometimes.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
